findings: ResetSeed gets application random and draws Next(0,20000000), constructs a separate ordinary System.Random, checks the current user session, then resets difficulty. Failure after ordinary seed creation retains that ordinary stream.

The attempt bank is lazily created from level number plus low32(userId) plus a cached device key, using native ushort shuffle and 1000 entries. The generated flag is set before the persisted attempt lookup; retries and level-number changes reuse the bank until user-cache invalidation.

DeviceIdKey caches nonzero values. The native parser starts from the empty string literal at0x55fc738, collects the first5 char.IsDigit UTF16 code units, then calls Int32.Parse; null/no digits/Unicode decimal parse failures propagate. SDK DeviceHelper.DeviceId transport is unchanged.

Bind removes then adds the same user-change handler. User cache reset clears remote/generated/switched flags while retaining streams/list/device/admin values. Clear ignores gameExit and only invalidates on an actual won level.

Restore performs two current-save lookups. After seeding, it stores the saved count and consumes Random.Next(1) exactly count times without adding to that count. Negative counts remain negative and consume nothing; ordinary random state is retained.

Unity fixture uses actual manager ResetSeed before context BindAll, actual application Unity random, and diagnostic level1/user1/device12345/attempt362 selecting seed371. Native permutation checksum244698400 confirms that diagnostic index. No production fake user/storage provider is installed.

performance.recommended: Preserve native sequential Next(1) replay for verified cursor fidelity. The tested normal cursor range is acceptable; any state-equivalent fast-forward alternative must be separately proven before adoption.
performance.cpu_loading: Replay is O(saved count), so very large cursors increase main-thread CPU and loading duration.
performance.gc_memory: No allocation per replay step; random reconstruction and the1000-entry bank are low-frequency fixed allocations. Do not cache an unbounded random sequence.
